normalized-weights.normalized-weight: Each weight is divided by the sum of all weights, so that the weights add up to 1.

extended-matrix.anti-ideal-benefit: For a benefit criterion the worst value is the smallest one in its column. It goes into the anti-ideal row (AAI).
extended-matrix.anti-ideal-cost: For a cost criterion the worst value is the largest one in its column. It goes into the anti-ideal row (AAI).
extended-matrix.ideal-benefit: For a benefit criterion the best value is the largest one in its column. It goes into the ideal row (AI).
extended-matrix.ideal-cost: For a cost criterion the best value is the smallest one in its column. It goes into the ideal row (AI).

normalized-matrix.benefit: A value of a benefit criterion is divided by the ideal value of that criterion. The closer the result is to 1, the closer the alternative is to the ideal.
normalized-matrix.cost: For a cost criterion the division is turned around: the ideal value is divided by the value. A lower cost gives a result closer to 1.

weighted-matrix.weighted: The normalized value is multiplied by the weight of its criterion, so important criteria count for more.

sums.sum: The weighted values of a row are added up. This is done for every alternative and also for the anti-ideal and ideal rows.

utility-degrees.k-minus: K⁻ compares an alternative with the anti-ideal solution: its sum divided by the sum of the anti-ideal row. Larger is better.
utility-degrees.k-plus: K⁺ compares an alternative with the ideal solution: its sum divided by the sum of the ideal row. The closer to 1, the closer to the ideal.

utility-functions.f-k-minus: The utility function in relation to the anti-ideal solution. Note the crossover: K⁺ is in the numerator.
utility-functions.f-k-plus: The utility function in relation to the ideal solution, with K⁻ in the numerator.

final-utility.final-utility: The final utility combines both utility degrees and both utility functions into one number. The highest value wins.

normalized-weights.normalized-weight: Each weight is divided by the sum of all weights, so that the weights add up to 1.

extended-matrix.anti-ideal-benefit: For a benefit criterion the anti-ideal value takes the smallest l, the smallest m and the smallest u of the column.
extended-matrix.anti-ideal-cost: For a cost criterion the anti-ideal value takes the largest l, the largest m and the largest u of the column.
extended-matrix.ideal-benefit: For a benefit criterion the ideal value takes the largest l, the largest m and the largest u of the column.
extended-matrix.ideal-cost: For a cost criterion the ideal value takes the smallest l, the smallest m and the smallest u of the column.

normalized-matrix.benefit: Each component of a benefit value is divided by one number: the upper value u of the ideal.
normalized-matrix.cost: For a cost criterion the lower value l of the ideal is divided by each component. The components swap places, so that l ≤ m ≤ u still holds.

weighted-matrix.weighted: The normalized fuzzy value is multiplied by the weight of its criterion, component by component.

sums.sum: The weighted fuzzy values of a row are added up component by component, for every alternative and for the anti-ideal and ideal rows.

utility-degrees.k-minus: K̃⁻ is the fuzzy sum of an alternative divided by the fuzzy sum of the anti-ideal row. In fuzzy division l is divided by u, m by m and u by l.
utility-degrees.k-plus: K̃⁺ is the fuzzy sum of an alternative divided by the fuzzy sum of the ideal row, with the same fuzzy division.

utility-degree-sums.t: The two fuzzy utility degrees of an alternative are added component by component.

max-utility-degree-sum.d: D̃ takes the largest l, the largest m and the largest u among all T̃.

max-utility-degree-sum-crisp.df: D̃ is turned into one crisp number with the graded mean. Every fuzzy utility function is divided by this number.

utility-functions.f-k-minus: The fuzzy utility function in relation to the anti-ideal solution: K̃⁺ divided by df_crisp. Note the crossover.
utility-functions.f-k-plus: The fuzzy utility function in relation to the ideal solution: K̃⁻ divided by df_crisp.

defuzzification.defuzzify: Each fuzzy utility degree and utility function is turned into one crisp number, so that the final utility can be calculated.

final-utility.final-utility: The final utility combines the crisp utility degrees and utility functions into one number. The highest value wins.

normalized-matrix.benefit: Each value of a benefit criterion is rescaled to the range 0 to 1: the worst value of the column becomes 0 and the best becomes 1.
normalized-matrix.cost: Each value of a cost criterion is rescaled to the range 0 to 1: the lowest value of the column becomes 1 and the highest becomes 0.

means.mean: The mean of each normalized column is the centre the deviations of the next step are measured from.

standard-deviations.sigma: The standard deviation of a normalized column measures its contrast intensity: the more the alternatives differ on a criterion, the larger it is.

correlation-matrix.pearson: The Pearson correlation of two criteria is the sum of the products of their deviations from the mean, divided by n times both standard deviations.

conflict.conflict: The conflict of a criterion adds up one minus its correlation with every criterion. A criterion that correlates little with the others carries more conflict.

information-content.information: The information content of a criterion is its standard deviation multiplied by its conflict.

weights.weight: Each information content is divided by the sum of all of them, so that the weights add up to 1.

normalized-matrix.benefit: For a benefit criterion the smallest value of the column is divided by the value, so the best performance gets 1 and smaller values get less.
normalized-matrix.cost: For a cost criterion the value is divided by the largest value of the column, so the best performance gets the smallest ratio.

absolute-logs.abs-ln: The absolute value of the natural logarithm of each normalized value measures how far it is from 1.

overall-performance.overall: The overall performance of an alternative is the logarithm of one plus the mean of its absolute logarithms.

removal-performance.removal: The performance is calculated again with one criterion left out. This is done for every alternative and every criterion.

removal-effects.effect: The removal effect of a criterion adds up how much the performance of each alternative changes when that criterion is left out.

weights.weight: Each removal effect is divided by the sum of all of them, so that the weights add up to 1.

coefficients.first: The most important criterion has the coefficient 1.
coefficients.coefficient: The coefficient of a criterion is its comparative importance, compared to the criterion before it, plus 1.

recalculated-weights.first: The most important criterion starts with the value 1.
recalculated-weights.recalculated: Each value is the value of the criterion before it divided by the coefficient of this criterion.

weights.weight: Each recalculated value is divided by the sum of all of them, so that the weights add up to 1.

coefficients.first: The most important criterion has the coefficient (1, 1, 1).
coefficients.coefficient: The coefficient of a criterion is its fuzzy comparative importance plus 1. Adding 1 moves the whole triangle to the right.

recalculated-weights.first: The most important criterion starts with the value (1, 1, 1).
recalculated-weights.recalculated: Each fuzzy value is the value of the criterion before it divided by the coefficient of this criterion.

recalculated-weights-sum.sum: The fuzzy values of all criteria are added up, component by component.

fuzzy-weights.weight: Each fuzzy value is divided by the fuzzy sum, so that the weights are fuzzy numbers that add up to about 1.

crisp-weights.defuzzify: Each fuzzy weight is turned into one number with the chosen defuzzification method.

weights.normalized: The defuzzified weights are divided by their sum, so that the crisp weights add up to 1.

playground.title: Fuzzy Playground
playground.hint: Drag the round handles of A and B, or use the arrow keys on a focused handle (Shift for bigger steps). Everything below is calculated by the fuzzy package.

chart.operands: Triangular fuzzy numbers A and B on the number line
chart.result: The result of the operation on the number line

operation.label: Operation
operation.scale: Multiply by a number  k · A

rule.add: The l, m and u values are added one by one.
rule.subtract: The lower value of A minus the upper value of B, the middle values subtracted, and the upper value of A minus the lower value of B.
rule.multiply: For positive numbers the l, m and u values are multiplied one by one.
rule.divide: For positive numbers: l of A divided by u of B, m by m, and u of A divided by l of B. B must not contain zero.
rule.scale: The l, m and u values are each multiplied by k.
rule.shift: The number k is added to l, m and u.

error.zero-divisor: B contains zero, so the quotient is not defined. Move B away from zero.
error.invalid: The result is not a valid triangular fuzzy number.
